title: HappyCamper download page
question: How does the download page get someone from landing to a running app with less text, emphasizing their likely OS and disclosing the rest on request?
settled: The download page is the hub. There is no separate landing page.
The page guesses the visitor's OS and offers the others in a picker.
Each OS gets one download button and its own install steps. Steps for other systems stay hidden.
The Apple Silicon steps are the model: download, open the .dmg, drag to Applications, open it, allow it once, then it opens normally.
The gatekeeper note says the warning is normal for apps outside the store, links the vendor's own guide, and points to Details.
What's new stays as the single 2.5 pill.
The page uses J's green paper, header bar and footer. Blue is the only second hue.
A's centered hero opens the page: logo, 'HappyCamper', the version and date, and the What's new pill. No tagline.
G's step band shows the install: one pictogram and a short caption per step.
The separate try-it section is gone. The header's Demo route is the only web demo link.
The OS picker is M's row: the likely module takes the width and the others shrink to a one- or two-word label. Versions and the 2021 threshold appear only once a module opens.
The macOS note reads: 'macOS requires these steps for any app not on the App Store. See Apple's guide for details. HappyCamper's code is open-source, learn more here.'
The bottom of the page is P's signpost cards: Demo in blue, Details in green, one line each, and the footer keeps only the credit.

The bottom cards read: Download demo rosters, 'Four sets of sample rosters to demo in the app.'; In-browser demo, 'The quickest look at HappyCamper's core features.'; Details, 'How the app is built, and how data is used.'
open: The install steps for each OS haven't been checked against a real install.

iterations.name: Original
iterations.tried: The live page before the trio: logo and title centered, four OS cards in a row with a recommended badge, one-line notes, and a sample data card. Pale paper and white cards.
iterations.why: The reference Jay prefers: modular, low text density.

iterations.name: Trio A
iterations.tried: The current redesign from 1120-page-trio: one white card with an OS dropdown, a collapsible five-step list, a reassurance box and a blue try box.
iterations.why: Serviceable, but chunky boxes exceed their content, the steps are dense bullets, and the white is harsh on the green.
contributed: the per-OS steps and trust links

iterations.name: Tiles and strip
iterations.tried: J's bar, paper and footer. Four small OS tiles, one download button, the steps as a row of numbered pictograms with three-word captions, the trust note in a Data Note box, and two small try tiles.
iterations.why: G preferred: only its band shows a helpful icon per step without over-depicting or under-explaining.

iterations.name: Evening, folded steps
iterations.tried: A dark forest palette. One panel holds OS pills, the button, and the steps folded behind a row of thumbnails that shows them before you open it. Try-it is one line of links.
iterations.why: G preferred: only its band shows a helpful icon per step without over-depicting or under-explaining.

iterations.name: Two columns, sage
iterations.tried: Soft sage paper. A sticky left column picks the OS and downloads; the right column is a rail of pictogram steps, with the trust note attached to the warning step it explains.
iterations.why: G preferred: only its band shows a helpful icon per step without over-depicting or under-explaining.

iterations.name: Install diagram
iterations.tried: J's look throughout. The install is one diagram in J's style: GitHub in an Internet box, then each step as a tile inside a Your Mac box, the warning step edged in amber, with a one-line caption and a First open note.
iterations.why: G preferred: only its band shows a helpful icon per step without over-depicting or under-explaining.

iterations.name: Four modules, canvas
iterations.tried: A warm canvas palette. The original's four OS cards return, shrunk to their content, each with its own button; choosing one shows its pictogram steps in a band under the row. Dashed try tiles.
iterations.why: The winner. Its tan paper, equal-width OS row and try-it section go; its pictogram band stays.

iterations.name: One step at a time
iterations.tried: A lake palette. Download is step one of a stepper; each step fills one panel with a large pictogram and a title, and only the warning step carries the trust note. Back, numbered dots, Next.
iterations.why: G preferred: only its band shows a helpful icon per step without over-depicting or under-explaining.

iterations.name: Featured card
iterations.tried: The likely OS as one centered G card with a 'For you' badge; the other three as small pills on an 'Other versions' line under it. Sample rosters as a blue '+ Sample rosters' line inside the card.
iterations.why: M preferred: it balances the likely option against the others without saturating the visitor.

iterations.name: Peeking tabs
iterations.tried: The likely OS card in front, the other three as icon tabs peeking from behind its right edge that slide open on hover. Sample rosters as a blue dashed tile at the end of the step band.
iterations.why: M preferred: it balances the likely option against the others without saturating the visitor.

iterations.name: Split button
iterations.tried: No card: one 'Download for Mac' button whose arrow opens the four versions, with the chip and file name under it. Sample rosters as a blue twin button beside it.
iterations.why: M preferred: it balances the likely option against the others without saturating the visitor.

iterations.name: Not right?
iterations.tried: The likely OS card alone, then a 'Not on a Mac, Apple Silicon? All versions' line that unfolds G's four-module row. Sample rosters as an 'Include sample rosters' checkbox that makes the button download both.
iterations.why: M preferred: it balances the likely option against the others without saturating the visitor.

iterations.name: Growing module
iterations.tried: G's row kept, but the likely module takes most of the width and the other three shrink to icon and name; clicking one grows it. Sample rosters as a blue pill beside What's new in the hero.
iterations.why: The winner. Collapsed modules shed their subtitles, the macOS note is rewritten, and the title becomes HappyCamper.

iterations.name: Short labels
iterations.tried: M with collapsed modules reading Mac (Silicon), Mac (Intel), Windows and Linux, no subtitles until a module opens, Jay's macOS note, and the title HappyCamper. Sample rosters stay a pill in the hero.
iterations.why: Not reviewed yet.

iterations.name: Samples column
iterations.tried: N with the sample rosters as a fifth, blue module instead of the hero pill. Opened, its band shows how to use them: unzip, import both, view and sort, export a CSV.
iterations.why: Base for P–S, which test a way to point at Demo and Details below the download.

iterations.name: Signpost cards
iterations.tried: O plus two cards under the band: Demo in blue with a globe, Details in green with a shield, each with one line. The footer drops its pills so each link appears once below the header.
iterations.why: The winner. Its signpost cards stay; the rosters return to the bottom beside them, and the guessed module needs a stronger highlight.

iterations.name: Footer lines
iterations.tried: O with no new section. The footer's Demo and Details pills move above the credit and each gains its one line.
iterations.why: P preferred.

iterations.name: Two questions
iterations.tried: O plus one aside box, darker than the page: 'Not ready to install? Try the demo…' and 'Questions about how it works, or why to trust it? See Details.' The footer drops its pills.
iterations.why: P preferred.

iterations.name: Picture tiles
iterations.tried: O plus two tiles, each a small drawing of the page it opens: the demo's table in a browser, and J's device diagram. One line each. The footer drops its pills.
iterations.why: P preferred.

iterations.name: Rosters box, clear guess
iterations.tried: P with the samples column removed and three cards at the bottom: Download demo rosters, In-browser demo and Details. The guessed module gets a solid green outline with a halo, a 'Suggested for you' badge and 'Guessed from your browser'; collapsed, it keeps a dashed green outline.
iterations.why: Shipped as site/index.html.
